newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt open to new Foncier formula.
newsitem.headline: French govt open to new Foncier formula.

text.p: The French government is open to any new proposals on troubled bank Credit Foncier and keeping a draft bill concerning the next stage of a contested wind-down on hold, government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said on Thursday.
Lamassoure told RTL radio mediator Philippe Rouvillois would contact unions at the occupied headquarters of Foncier at 0730 GMT to get talks going on day seven of the occupation.

"At 0830 (local) the mediator appointed by the government will make contact with the unions and if there is a formula other than the one on the table at the moment, we are fully open to negotiation," he said.

"In the meantime, and this is very important, the draft law which was prepared by the government to save the trade... and avoid all straight layoffs at Credit Foncier is being kept in waiting," Lamassoure said.

Lamassoure kept up the government line that there was no hard-and-fast government plan but that the taxpayer would not be asked to foot the bill for a state cash injection and that there was only one offer open to it at the moment, a partial takeover by cooperatively run Credit Immobilier.

The legislation in question would set up a state holding company into which it would spin off the part of Credit Foncier not taken over by Credit Immobilier, with a view to winding it down over the coming years.

The unions decided on Wednesday to release chairman Jerome Meyssonnier and seven board members prevented from leaving the Paris headquarters where hundreds of employees are keeping vigil since last Friday in their compaign to prevent this plan being put into action pending the search for an alternative.
Lamassoure's comments, while still far from clear-cut, were the clearest indication to date the government appeared to be taking a softer, more conciliatory line.
